legitimateExplanations.title: Total loss of position data.
legitimateExplanations.actually: Genuine coverage failure, tunnel or terrain shadowing, hardware fault, SIM or data plan failure, or regional interference not directed at this vehicle.
legitimateExplanations.ruleOut: Check whether other vehicles in the same area and time lost signal too. Broad regional loss indicates environmental or infrastructure causes; an isolated single-vehicle gap does not.

legitimateExplanations.title: Implausible position jumps.
legitimateExplanations.actually: Known receiver artefacts, cold-start errors, multipath in urban canyons, or platform data-processing lag.
legitimateExplanations.ruleOut: Check whether the artefact appears across the fleet on the same hardware and firmware, which points to a technical rather than deliberate cause.

legitimateExplanations.title: Sustained regional GNSS interference.
legitimateExplanations.actually: Documented wide-area interference affecting all users in a region, which is well reported in parts of Europe and is not aimed at any particular vehicle.
legitimateExplanations.ruleOut: Compare against published interference monitoring for the region and period before drawing any conclusion about a specific movement.

legitimateExplanations.title: A tracker goes silent at a terminal or after a short stop.
legitimateExplanations.actually: Battery failure, planned maintenance, coverage loss, wiring fault or a device replaced during a legitimate repair.
legitimateExplanations.ruleOut: Compare with fleet-wide outages, inspect the device and wiring, and reconcile the movement with independent records before attributing intent.

countermeasures.text: Run automated speed and distance plausibility checks between consecutive fixes and alert on physically impossible transitions.
Inspect and photograph the telematics installation before the vehicle re-enters service, since physical evidence of tampering disappears quickly.
